summary: New Era Energy & Digital, a data center developer, moves to intervene in EL26-67 and files limited comments asking PJM to address a Maximum Net Withdrawal study framework and fast-track treatment of uprates and reactivated capacity in its adequacy report.
ask: Grant intervention and have PJM address Maximum Net Withdrawal for paired load and generation, and expedited uprate and reactivation pathways, in its forthcoming filings.

points.point: New Era says PJM should study a load paired with dependable nearby generation by its enforceable maximum net withdrawal rather than full gross demand.
points.quote: PJM should evaluate the project based on the facility’s enforceable maximum net withdrawal from the transmission system, rather than assuming the facility will impose its full gross demand

points.point: A net-withdrawal cap would need metering, controls, operator visibility and tariff consequences for exceedance.
points.quote: a binding net-withdrawal cap in the relevant service agreement or other tariff- governed arrangement

points.point: PJM should say what transmission service an Eligible Customer takes for a load operated under such a cap.
points.quote: PJM should also explain what transmission service the Eligible Customer must take for a large load operated subject to an enforceable Maximum Net Withdrawal.

points.point: The 30-day adequacy report should cover expedited study of low-risk uprates at existing plants.
points.quote: PJM should address whether its Tariff provides an adequate pathway for expedited treatment of uprates at existing generating facilities.

points.point: It also asks about expedited reconnection of retired or mothballed capacity without bypassing reliability review.
points.quote: The purpose would not be to bypass reliability review, but to avoid subjecting bounded reactivations of existing capacity to procedures designed for wholly new speculative projects.

throughLine.text: Limited comments on E-7 asking PJM to address proximate-generation study treatment in its show cause response and uprate fast-tracking in the 30-day adequacy report.

figures.label: PJM forecast peak load growth 2024 to 2030, as described by New Era
figures.quote: PJM’s load forecast predicts peak load growth of 32 GW from 2024 to 2030, with 30 GW of that growth projected to come from data centers.
